title: Farm land subdivision lessee notice bill
summary: On September 16 the commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the County Council bill on farm land subdivision notice, with the Planning Department's amendments, after a first motion fell one vote short. The bill would require owners to notify lessees by certified mail at least 10 business days before applying, and the department wants the rule moved to Title 18. It goes to the Molokaʻi Planning Commission next week, and staff will take all three commissions' recommendations to the council.

timeline.text: Commissioners asked that the council also consider notice for residential and commercial land.

Second motion to recommend approval of the agricultural subdivision notice bill with the department's recommended amendments: The commission voted to recommend approval of the bill with the department's recommended amendments.
Motion to defer action on the agricultural subdivision notice bill: A motion to defer the bill to get more information from the council died because no one seconded it.

First motion to recommend approval of the agricultural subdivision notice bill with the department's recommended amendments: The first motion to approve got four votes and did not pass because five were needed.
Staff will take all three planning commissions' recommendations to the council before it decides.
The Planning Department recommended moving the rule to Title 18, the County's subdivision code.
Owners would have to notify lessees (people renting the land) by certified mail at least 10 business days before applying.
The bill goes to the Molokaʻi Planning Commission next week.
The commission held a public hearing on a County Council bill about farm land subdivisions.
Next month's agenda includes County Council resolution 26-68, which would require notice to lessees when agricultural land is subdivided.
